title: 1 Samuel 5 — The ark of the Elohim among the Pelishtim (Philistines)

verdicts.reasoning: ûp̄əlištîm lāqəḥû ʾēṯ ʾărôn hāʾĕlōhîm: pluperfect 'had taken'; articular 'the ark of the Elohim' (clause 1). Exact.

Re-parsed: wəhinnēh dāḡôn nōp̄ēl ləp̄ānāyw ʾarṣâ lip̄nê ʾărôn YHWH. 'had fallen on his face to the ground' is literal; the note reads the posture as prostration (McCarter), which is the standard interpretation. The reception note (electrical discharge, transmitter-receiver with atomic battery) accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 and the line encodes nothing of it.

paragraphs.text: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לָֽקְח֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְבִאֻ֛הוּ מֵאֶ֥בֶן הָעֵ֖זֶר אַשְׁדּֽוֹדָה׃

i18n.en: Now the Pelishtim had taken the ark of the Elohim, and they brought it from Even-Ha'ezer to Ashdod.

notes.official: *ʾărôn hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the ark of the Elohim': the Hebrew has the article (clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). The chapter alternates 'the ark of the Elohim', 'the ark of YHWH' (vv 3, 4) and, in the speech of the Pelishtim, 'the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el' (vv 7, 8, 10, 11), as the Hebrew does (proposed central `aron-ark-of-the-covenant-ark-of-the-elohim-cross-corpus`). Even-Ha'ezer = Eben-ezer ('stone of help', 4:1; 7:12); Ashdod; Pelishtim = Philistines (central `pelishtim-caphtor`) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְח֤וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֣ית דָּג֑וֹן וַיַּצִּ֥יגוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֵ֥צֶל דָּגֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the Pelishtim took the ark of the Elohim and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.

notes.official: *bêṯ dāḡôn* 'the house of Dagon', his temple. Dagon is the West-Semitic god Dagan, whose name is generally connected with *dāḡān* 'grain' and whom the Pelishtim adopted (proposed central `dagon-philistine-deity-hebrew-bible-cross-corpus`, with the Ugaritic sibling `dagan-dagon-grain-deity-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible-philistine-pantheon`); the derivation from *dāḡ* 'fish' is a later folk etymology. *wayyaṣṣîḡû ʾōṯô ʾēṣel dāḡôn* 'and set it beside Dagon', as a trophy in the god's house.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֤מוּ אַשְׁדּוֹדִים֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־דָּג֔וֹן וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And when the Ashdodites rose early on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH. And they took Dagon and set him back in his place.

notes.official:
*wayyaškimû ʾašdôḏîm* 'And when the Ashdodites rose early' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *wəhinnēh dāḡôn nōp̄ēl ləp̄ānāyw ʾarṣâ* 'behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground', the posture of prostration before a superior: the image bows to the ark (McCarter, *I Samuel*). *ʾărôn YHWH* 'the ark of YHWH' (`aron-ark-of-the-covenant-ark-of-the-elohim-cross-corpus`; `dagon-philistine-deity-hebrew-bible-cross-corpus`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) reads 1 Sam 5:1-5 as an electrical discharge from the 'ark of God', which it describes as housing a transmitter-receiver with its own atomic battery, set off by the Pelishtim's mishandling. The line renders *nōp̄ēl ... ʾarṣâ* literally ('had fallen on his face to the ground') and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּקֶר֮ מִֽמָּחֳרָת֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וְרֹ֨אשׁ דָּג֜וֹן וּשְׁתֵּ֣י ׀ כַּפּ֣וֹת יָדָ֗יו כְּרֻתוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּפְתָּ֔ן רַ֥ק דָּג֖וֹן נִשְׁאַ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And when they rose early in the morning on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold; only Dagon was left to him.

notes.official: On the second morning Dagon has fallen again, and his head and both palms lie *kərūṯôṯ ʾel-hammip̄tān* 'cut off on the threshold' (`mifthan-ha-bayit`). *raq dāḡôn nišʾar ʿālāyw* 'only Dagon was left to him' (MT): the sense is that only the body of the image remained. The ASV supplies '[the stump of]', and many emend after the LXX ('the spine of Dagon') to *gēwô* 'his trunk' (Driver, *Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel*, 1913; McCarter). The MT is translated without supplement (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). The image of a fish-tailed Dagon was later read into this half-verse; the Hebrew does not describe the image's form (`dagon-philistine-deity-hebrew-bible-cross-corpus`). The reception note at v 3 applies.

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יִדְרְכוּ֩ כֹהֲנֵ֨י דָג֜וֹן וְכָֽל־הַבָּאִ֧ים בֵּית־דָּג֛וֹן עַל־מִפְתַּ֥ן דָּג֖וֹן בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Therefore the priests of Dagon, and all who come into the house of Dagon, do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, unto this day.

notes.official: *ʿal-kēn lōʾ-yiḏrəḵû ... ʿal-mip̄tan dāḡôn* 'Therefore ... do not tread on the threshold of Dagon' (`mifthan-ha-bayit`; `ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`): an aetiology for the custom of stepping over a sanctuary threshold (cf. Zeph 1:9).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּכְבַּ֧ד יַד־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הָאַשְׁדּוֹדִ֖ים וַיְשִׁמֵּ֑ם וַיַּ֤ךְ אֹתָם֙ בעפלים [בַּטְּחֹרִ֔ים] אֶת־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וְאֶת־גְּבוּלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And the hand of YHWH was heavy on the Ashdodites, and he devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territory.

notes.official:
*wattiḵbaḏ yaḏ-YHWH* 'And the hand of YHWH was heavy' (`yad-yhwh`), the recurring phrase of the ark narrative (vv 6, 7, 9, 11; 6:3, 5, 9). *wayšimmēm* 'and he devastated them' (ASV 'destroyed'). *wayyaḵ ʾōṯām baṭṭəḥōrîm* 'and struck them with tumors' translates the Qere *ṭəḥōrîm*. The Ketiv *ʿŏp̄ālîm* means 'swellings, mounds'; the Talmud lists it among words read with a substitute for delicacy (b. Megillah 25b). The KJV has 'emerods' (haemorrhoids), as does the English quotation in the canon; the French has 'bubons'. The nature of the affliction is disputed: haemorrhoids in rabbinic tradition, the buboes of bubonic plague in many modern readings, given the rodents of 6:4-5 (`ofalim-tehorim-tumors-1-samuel-5-6`; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). After this verse the LXX adds that mice swarmed in the land and there was a great deadly panic; that plus is not translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('He smote them with emerods') and reads the affliction as burns caused by radiation from radioactive material in the ark. The line translates the Masoretic reading as 'tumors' and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד כִּֽי־כֵ֑ן וְאָמְר֗וּ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֞ב אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־קָשְׁתָ֤ה יָדוֹ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַ֖ל דָּג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: And when the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, "The ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el shall not remain with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our elohim."

notes.official: *lōʾ-yēšēḇ ʾărôn ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl ʿimmānû* 'The ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el shall not remain with us' (`elohei-yisrael`; clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`); *ʿal dāḡôn ʾĕlōhênû* 'on Dagon our elohim', lower case for the Pelishti god (clause 4). *kî-qāšəṯâ yāḏô* 'for his hand is severe'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֡וּ וַיַּאַסְפוּ֩ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֗ה לַֽאֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ גַּ֣ת יִסֹּ֔ב אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּסֵּ֕בּוּ אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Pelishtim to them, and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el?" And they said, "Let the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el be carried around to Gat." And they carried the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el around.

notes.official: *sarnê p̄əlištîm* 'the lords of the Pelishtim' (ASV): *seren* is the title of the rulers of the five Pelishti cities, a non-Semitic word often compared with Greek *tyrannos* (`seranim-lords-of-the-pelishtim-1-samuel`). *gaṯ yissōḇ* 'be carried around to Gat' (Gat = Gath).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֞י אַחֲרֵ֣י ׀ הֵסַ֣בּוּ אֹת֗וֹ וַתְּהִ֨י יַד־יְהוָ֤ה ׀ בָּעִיר֙ מְהוּמָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּשָּׂתְר֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם עפלים [טְחֹרִֽים׃]

i18n.en: And it came to pass, after they had carried it around, that the hand of YHWH was against the city with a very great panic; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great, and tumors broke out on them.

notes.official: *məhûmâ gəḏôlâ məʾōḏ* 'a very great panic' (cf. Josh 10:10, *hmm*). *wayyiśśāṯərû lāhem ṭəḥōrîm* 'and tumors broke out on them': Qere *ṭəḥōrîm*, Ketiv *ʿplym* (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`; `ofalim-tehorim-tumors-1-samuel-5-6`); the verb *wayyiśśāṯərû* occurs only here, and 'broke out' renders it from the context. *miqqāṭōn wəʿaḏ-gāḏôl* 'both small and great'.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עֶקְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֗י כְּב֨וֹא אֲר֤וֹן הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עֶקְר֔וֹן וַיִּזְעֲק֨וּ הָֽעֶקְרֹנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר הֵסַ֤בּוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־אֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נִי וְאֶת־עַמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: So they sent the ark of the Elohim to Eqron. And it came to pass, as the ark of the Elohim came to Eqron, that the Eqronites cried out, saying, "They have carried around to me the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el, to kill me and my people."

notes.official: Eqron = Ekron; *hāʿeqrōnîm* 'the Eqronites' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *hēsabbû ʾēlay* 'They have carried around to me': the city speaks in the singular ('to kill me and my people').

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ וַיַּאַסְפ֜וּ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לִמְקֹמ֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֖י וְאֶת־עַמִּ֑י כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה מְהֽוּמַת־מָ֙וֶת֙ בְּכָל־הָעִ֔יר כָּבְדָ֥ה מְאֹ֛ד יַ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Pelishtim, and they said, "Send away the ark of the Elohim of Yisra'el, and let it return to its own place, that it may not kill me and my people." For there was a deadly panic throughout all the city; the hand of the Elohim was very heavy there.

notes.official: *məhûmaṯ-māweṯ* 'a deadly panic'; *yaḏ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the hand of the Elohim' (articular, clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). The lords of the Pelishtim (`seranim-lords-of-the-pelishtim-1-samuel`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מֵ֔תוּ הֻכּ֖וּ בעפלים [בַּטְּחֹרִ֑ים] וַתַּ֛עַל שַֽׁוְעַ֥ת הָעִ֖יר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the men who did not die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

notes.official: *wəhāʾănāšîm ʾăšer lōʾ-meṯû hukkû baṭṭəḥōrîm* 'And the men who did not die were struck with the tumors' (Qere; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`; `ofalim-tehorim-tumors-1-samuel-5-6`). *wattaʿal šawʿaṯ hāʿîr haššāmāyim* 'and the cry of the city went up to the heavens': a cry for help rising to the divine realm (cf. Ex 2:23), so *šāmayim* is 'heavens' under the register clause of central `shamayim` (ASV 'to heaven').
